method: Direct inspection of user-supplied Kehot publisher scan; page images and extracted text checked together. No blocked crawler was used.
identity_relation: All ten letters enrich existing index identities. Letters ד׳שס and ד׳שסח had conservative exception identities. Same-page OCR identities ד׳שם, ד׳שטג, ד׳שטה and ד׳שטו are resolved to ד׳שס, ד׳שסג, ד׳שסה and ד׳שסו rather than counted again. Duplicate later index rows for several spellings are metadata artifacts, not additional witnesses.

evidence_family_dedup.counting_rule: The letter responds to the already documented Kfar Chabad attack and joins that event-level family; it is a distinct letter witness, not a new attack or recovery campaign.

Letter ד׳שסד explicitly continues the same practical-halacha class correspondence documented in ד׳רצו. Both letters therefore share one evidence family; the follow-up is a distinct letter witness, not an independent case.
The Lag BaOmer paragraph is a related facet inside a broader fundraising and school-branch letter; it does not create a separate campaign witness.

blocked_alternatives.result: Previously documented HTTP 403/item-shell failures; data/acquisition/latest.json reports no candidates and no enriched records in the latest run.
blocked_alternatives.action: Known blocked routes were not retried; the user-supplied publisher scan was used as the accessible source.

rights_boundary: No complete letter text is reproduced. Only bounded non-verbatim research paraphrases, locators, provenance, context and limitations are stored.
